label: the shipped graphics profiles, flying out of the loaded world
comment: The third of the profile plans. profiles.json and profiles-night.json
both measure a settled world with the camera still, which is the
kindest possible case for settings whose whole job is limiting how
much world is streamed: the cost of a bigger view lands while it
arrives, not once it has. This is the plan that makes it arrive.
The route flies a long way out, one way, so the client is always
entering ground it has not seen. Two things follow from that and are
deliberate:
No GOANNA_STORE. Every other profile plan points one at a warm store,
because a cold store never converges at the vista and the steady state
would be measured on a world still arriving. Here that is the point,
so each run gets the fresh XDG_DATA_HOME the harness makes for it and
therefore its own cold store. That is also what makes a process per
variant honest here: the failure this plan replaces shared one warm
store between processes, the store filled as the plan ran, each tier
started from a fuller world than the last, and the end of plan control
repeat came back 45.7 per cent from the first on the steady median.
Cold and identical beats warm and shared.
move_early only, not move_full. move_full ramps the speed until the
terrain stops keeping up, and decides that with ground_fraction, which
counts samples where the client found ground under the camera. The
ground scan gives up when the camera is far above the terrain (main.gd
holds terrain_ref at its last answer while flying too high), so at any
altitude that clears the hills every tier reports a top speed of zero
and the table says nothing. Measured that way once: 3 per cent ground
at walking pace, on every tier. Flying low enough to fix it means
flying into things. move_early asks the question that survives: set
off the moment the world is playable and see whether it holds.
The route is absolute, not relative, so every variant flies the same
ground rather than a path relative to wherever it happened to spawn.
y is a fixed 120, well above anything in this part of test_world:
the village sits near 30 and the vista anchor at 54. Fly mode moves
the camera without collision, so a peak taller than the route does not
stop the run, it just spends that leg inside a hill and measures
nothing useful. Altitude is the first thing to change if this world's
terrain gets taller.
At 40 nodes a second for 60 seconds the camera covers about 2400
nodes. The largest far distance any tier asks for is 2048 and the
widest view range is 16 mapblocks, so the flight leaves everything it
started with well behind it.
